A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T-SAC work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support comparison; retained material was matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original T-SAC experiments on Meta-World, five MuJoCo tasks and dense/sparse Box-Pushing, together with architectural and training ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional Walker2d sensitivity and robustness results, revised sparse-reward experiments and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The Transformer architecture, multi-horizon gradient loss and one-step actor remain. The sparse-reward configuration is refined: v3 Section 4.4 recommends conventional target updates after hard-copy instability, whereas v4 reports stable hard-copy training using a minimum-of-two-Q target (Appendix F). This is a localized target-construction/update refinement.

E1.justification: The same 57 benchmark tasks remain. v4 Figure 4i adds distinct Walker2d scenarios with action noise, state noise, stochastic termination and removal of half the observation, extending evaluation to perturbed input and environment conditions.

E2.justification: TOP-ERL is newly included in the computational-cost comparison in v4 Table 3; v3 Figure 2 compared T-SAC, SAC, CrossQ, GRU and LSTM. Those earlier timing comparisons remain in v4 Figure 12. The principal benchmark baseline sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 adds freezing-interval and horizon sweeps, specified perturbation protocols, performance-threshold measurements and computational evaluations. Existing settings also change: the sparse Box-Pushing critic learning rate rises from 2.5e-5 to 3.0e-4, while Hopper/Walker2d initialization changes from log-standard-deviation -10 to -5 and target entropy from -4 times action dimension to the SAC default. These are reported setting revisions, not merely additional documentation.

E4.justification: v4 adds Walker2d tests of freezing interval, supervision horizon and robustness (Figure 4g-i), plus sequence-length versus computational-cost analysis (Table 2). The sparse-reward appendix comparison changes from hard versus soft updates to minimum versus randomly selected double-Q targets. Earlier Box-Pushing component, chunking, sampling and recurrent-critic ablations remain.

E5.justification: v4 Tables 2 and 4 introduce mean-plus-standard-error reporting alongside the retained IQM/bootstrap-confidence-interval practice. The general eight-seed and four-seed-ablation statements and baseline-specific seed counts remain; the PDFs do not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: The Hopper and Walker2d T-SAC curves are replaced, and sparse Box-Pushing success changes from 58% to a reported 60% with hard-copy training. These accompany changed settings and should not be interpreted as same-setting gains. v4 also adds sensitivity, robustness, memory, parameter-count and efficiency results. Meta-World curves, dense Box-Pushing's 96.8% headline and the original six ablation panels remain.

T1.justification: New Section 4.1.3 and Appendix E introduce an extended-action MDP construction, Proposition 6 on conditional unbiasedness and a relationship to the ordinary action-value. v3 Appendix G's shared-bootstrap reuse and quadratic sparse-reward amplification argument is replaced in v4 Appendix H by fixed-start, multi-horizon reasoning with linear E[L] amplification. The variance proofs in Appendices C and D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains critic-side sequence modeling with multi-step supervision and one-step policy updates. The abstract and Section 4.4 broaden the hard-copy stability claim from local-motion benchmarks to multiple benchmarks, explicitly including sparse Box-Pushing.

C2.justification: v4 attributes sparse hard-copy instability to random target selection and reverses the earlier suggestion that episode-boundary masking may degrade performance. It revises the chunking mechanism explanation and adds explicit limits concerning low-dimensional online continuous control and difficult pixel/discrete/partially observable extensions. New robustness prose also claims advantages over SAC and CrossQ, although Figure 4i displays only T-SAC variants.

D1.justification: v3 promises a future code release; v4 provides repository and experiment-dashboard links and reports releasing scripts, configurations, logs and artifacts. It also adds parameter counts, peak GPU memory, detailed timing information and explanations of segment packing, masking and target caching. The Q-chunking baseline's omission of offline behavior cloning is newly documented, without establishing a change from v3's implementation.

R1.justification: v4 expands the distinction from offline Decision Transformer policies and discusses S2AC/DIME as complementary actor-side approaches. S2AC is newly cited; the Transformer survey, TransDreamer and action-repetition references are removed. The main positioning relative to TOP-ERL, CrossQ and Q-chunking remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten and reorganized, TOP-ERL discussion moves into related work, and numbered ablation subsections become run-in discussions. The segment-analysis appendix is reorganized and rewritten. v4 also expands the conclusion and moves the LLM disclosure before references alongside new ethics, contribution and acknowledgment sections.

P2.justification: v4 adds four quantitative tables and expands the main ablation figure from six to nine panels. The locomotion plots are rearranged into one row, benchmark legends and panel placement change, and schematic arrows/labels are redrawn. The unchanged timing chart moves to Appendix I; most existing appendix figures and hyperparameter-table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves transparency through additional sensitivity/cost analyses, reported code/log access and a propagation derivation better aligned with the fixed-start loss. However, new robustness superiority claims lack corresponding SAC/CrossQ results in Figure 4i, and Proposition 6 does not justify equating conditioning on feedback-generated replay actions with open-loop execution. These benefits coexist with weaknesses in the new empirical interpretations and theoretical guarantee, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
